territorial_scope.description: Adds a section to the California Government Code, so it governs committees and advertisements subject to the California Political Reform Act.

evidence.quote: If a committee, as defined in Section 82013, creates, originally publishes, or originally distributes a qualified political advertisement

summary.short: Adds Gov. Code § 84514: committees that create, originally publish or distribute a qualified political advertisement containing AI-generated or substantially altered image, audio or video must include a prescribed AI disclosure. The Commission may seek injunctive relief or pursue administrative or civil remedies for non-compliance.
summary.long: Adds Government Code section 84514 to the Political Reform Act of 1974. Under subdivision (a), a committee, as defined in Section 82013, that creates, originally publishes or originally distributes a qualified political advertisement must include the disclosure “Ad generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence” in a clear and conspicuous manner, displayed or spoken as prescribed in Sections 84504 to 84504.5, as applicable. A qualified political advertisement is one containing any image, audio or video generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence. Media is entirely created by AI if it would falsely appear authentic to a reasonable person, or materially altered if the alteration would give a reasonable person a fundamentally different understanding; immaterial alterations such as cosmetic adjustments, colour edits, cropping or resizing are excluded. If a committee does not comply, the Commission may seek injunctive relief under Section 90009 or pursue administrative or civil remedies under Chapter 3 or Chapter 11, but a violation is not a misdemeanor. The section does not alter rights, obligations or immunities of interactive service providers under 47 U.S.C. Section 230. The text states no effective date of its own.

notes: Excerpt: this document contains only SEC. 8 (new Gov. Code Sec. 84514) of AB 2355; the rest of the bill, its enactment date and its chapter number are not in the text. Subdivision (a)(2) incorporates display and spoken-disclosure rules in Secs. 84504 to 84504.5, and subdivision (c) relies on Secs. 90009, 83100 et seq. and 91000 et seq.; none of these are included, so their content is not annotated. The terms 'committee' (Sec. 82013) and 'Commission' are defined outside this excerpt. The text states no penalty amount; subdivision (c)(2) says a violation is not a misdemeanor. Subdivision (c)(1) makes Commission action discretionary ('may take either of the following actions').

events.note: The provided text is Sec. 8 only (adding Government Code 84514). It states no dates, and no signature, publication, entry-into-force, application or sunset date appears in the document.

thresholds.note: The annotated provisions (Gov. Code § 84514, added by SEC. 8) contain no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. The numbers that appear are statutory section and chapter references (84504, 83100, 91000, 90009, 230 of Title 47) and enumeration labels. The definition of 'qualified political advertisement' turns on whether media is generated or substantially altered by AI, not on a numeric value.
